title: Honeybee eggs · seasonal molecular patterns
pairing_unit: Exact queen ID shared by the lipid-positive and metabolite-positive/negative source tables and queen metadata. Queen identity links egg pools across assays.

views.name: Metabolomics
views.unit: log₂ LC–MS peak intensity; positive + negative modes

papers.title: Honey bee egg composition changes seasonally and after acute maternal virus infection

processing: Keep the exact queen-ID intersection of the three source LC-MS sheets and queen metadata. Preserve all unambiguously matched queens.
Group by published collection month (May versus June), not by an omics-derived outcome. Preserve continuous collection_day and published log virus load for exploratory factor associations.

Combine positive and negative metabolite modes as a single view with distinct feature IDs; use lipid positive mode as the second molecular view. The views can include related chemical signals and are not independent technologies.
Positive peak areas are log2 transformed; zero intensity is marked missing. No artificial values or new imputation are added. Preserve source feature-row IDs and putative compound labels.
Filter features with more than 50% missingness or zero variance; retain at most 1200 variable features per layer without group labels.

teaching.description: Explore how egg lipid and metabolite profiles vary across May and June. Two molecular layers share the same queen identities.
teaching.warning: Two measured views: lipidomics and metabolomics. Positive/negative metabolite ion modes are combined into one layer. Month is an observational seasonal comparison; collection date, beekeeper and environment can covary. Source compound labels are putative annotations. Human GO/KEGG catalogs are not applied to these bee features.
